newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: F&P expects to match 1995/96 year profit.
newsitem.headline: F&P expects to match 1995/96 year profit.

text.p: Domestic appliance manufacturer Fisher and Paykel Industries on Wednesday said it anticipated a full year profit similar to, if not slightly better than, last year's result of NZ$39.25 million.
Earlier, F&P reported a profit for the six months to September 30, 1996, of NZ$19.2 million, against NZ$19.4 million in the corresponding period last year.

"The directors believe the trends experienced in the six months to September 30 will continue in the second half of the financial year, and anticipate a similar if not slightly improved result to last year," F&P said in a statement.
Fisher & Paykel had made significant progress in "cost innovation", and in its ability to react quickly to changes in business and market conditions.
"This has helped to alleviate the adverse impact on profit caused by the appreciation of the NZ dollar."
Whiteware competition in New Zealand, Australia and other export markets had continued to intensify. With slower economic growth, market sizes for most products had also reduced.
F&P declared a fully imputed interim dividend of nine cents per share. Shareholders who had so elected would receive shares in lieu of the dividend.

A discount of 10 percent of the weighted average price in the next five trading days would be used in calculating share entitlements. Qualifying non-resident shareholders would receive a supplementary dividend of 1.59 cents per share.
